title: Claude 4.5 Sonnet released
body: Today we're releasing Claude 4.5 Sonnet, our new state-of-the-art model. It scores 82.1% on SWE-bench Verified, up from 74.3% for the previous version. On MMLU it reaches 89.4%. Pricing is $3 / M input tokens and $15 / M output tokens — a 40% reduction versus Claude 3.5 Sonnet at launch. The model is available today via the API, on Amazon Bedrock, and on Google Cloud Vertex AI. Rate limits for Tier 1 customers doubled to 100,000 tokens per minute.

title: Sparse autoencoders find interpretable features in Gemma-2
body: We trained sparse autoencoders (SAEs) with 262k features on residual stream activations at layer 20 of Gemma-2-9B. Each SAE decoder direction corresponds to a monosemantic feature — examples include 'legal terminology', 'code error messages', and 'refusal to answer'. Using activation patching, we causally verified that ablating the 'refusal' feature reduces refusal rate on harmful prompts by 42%. The paper open-sources all SAE weights and a browser-based feature visualizer.

title: Building AI agents at scale — with Yohei Nakajima
body: so um welcome back to the podcast. today we have Yohei who created BabyAGI. hey Yohei thanks for coming on. so tell us a bit about your background before AI. yeah so I was working in VC and I got into AI in early 2023. right so tell us about BabyAGI. so BabyAGI is basically a task loop — you give it a goal, it decomposes into subtasks, executes them, and adds new tasks. the core insight was that you don't need fancy planning, just a while loop and an LLM. we saw people extend it in tons of directions. one issue though is that agents get stuck in loops and burn tokens. we've been experimenting with a 'task priority queue' plus a critic model that scores whether each task actually made progress. early results — task completion up 3x, token usage down 40%.

title: Meta releases Llama 5 400B
body: Meta released Llama 5 today, a 400B parameter MoE model with 40B active parameters. On MMLU it scores 91.2%, matching GPT-4o. However the license restricts commercial use to organizations under 700M monthly active users — Meta's usual carve-out to exclude the largest cloud providers. Weights are hosted on Hugging Face and require accepting the license. Serving the full model requires 8xH100 minimum.
